name: Duskline MA-2 Bomber
description:
A straight military-silhouette bomber in matte sage green nylon with a knit collar, cuffs, and waistband in charcoal grey. The shell is a medium-weight ripstop with a quilted poly lining visible when the front zipper opens — warm, not hot, the kind of jacket that works from September through November before you need something heavier. Duskline is a Tier 2 street brand operating out of a converted warehouse in the South Shelf transition zone, known for clean military-adjacent pieces at prices that don't require a payment plan.

The MA-2 is their bestseller and has been for eleven years running. No patches, no branding beyond a small embroidered logo on the inner pocket. It's the jacket you wear when you want to look put-together without looking like you're trying. Mechanics, students, off-shift security workers, and junior creatives all reach for it.
what_it_says: You know what you like and you found a brand that delivers it. Unfussy, practical, quietly stylish.
story_hooks: A specific run of Duskline MA-2s from three years ago was manufactured using a fabric batch that subtly interferes with certain biometric scanners — wearers have been passing checkpoints they shouldn't.
Someone has been leaving Duskline MA-2s at locations where Shelf-district crimes have occurred — different sizes, all identical, all with the inner pocket torn out.

The Duskline warehouse is being pressured by a corponation that wants to acquire the brand — the founders are looking for someone to help them disappear the master patterns and tooling before the buyout goes through.

physical_description.visual_profile: Structured military bomber with a clean, unfussy silhouette. Straight-cut through the torso with a slight taper at the waist. The matte sage green reads professional without pretension — the kind of jacket that disappears into a crowd but holds its own on inspection. Knit collar sits high and defined; cuffs and waistband create subtle articulation.
physical_description.fit: True straight military cut — not oversized, not fitted. Shoulders sit natural, sleeves taper gently to the wrist. Waistband cinches without compression. Built for layering over light base layers or worn alone over a fitted tee.
physical_description.primary_material: Medium-weight nylon ripstop shell with quilted polyester lining. The nylon has a subtle matte finish — no shine, no sheen. Practical and durable without looking industrial.
physical_description.texture: Shell surface is smooth with fine grid texture from ripstop weave. Knit collar, cuffs, and waistband are soft charcoal grey with visible ribbing. Quilted lining creates subtle dimensionality when visible through the open front.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte sage green (primary) with charcoal grey knit trim. No patterns. The two-color blocking is understated and versatile.
physical_description.closures: Center-front metal zipper, likely Φ-grade industrial-spec. Smooth operation, visible metal slider.
distinctive_features: Knit collar, cuffs, and waistband in contrasting charcoal grey
Medium-weight quilted poly lining visible on interior
Small embroidered Duskline logo on inner pocket — no external branding
Ripstop nylon shell with subtle grid texture
Straight military silhouette with subtle waist definition
Functional simplicity — no excess hardware, no patch pockets beyond essentials
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2 accessible luxury — quality construction and materials at non-premium pricing. The kind of piece that signals taste and practicality, not wealth.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street professional. Worn by mechanics who need durability, junior corpo creatives who value substance over logos, students building functional wardrobes, and off-shift security workers who want to look human outside the uniform. Associated with Duskline's South Shelf warehouse community — understated, locally-rooted, built for real use.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but maintained. After a season or two of regular wear, the nylon develops a subtle patina and the knit trim may show minor pilling at high-friction points. Owners tend to take care of these jackets — they're built to last and the investment justifies it.
